propositions: Errored pairs are currently counted as decision flips without an errored guard, causing a single transient runtime error to incorrectly trigger a model-quality regression in criterion (b)

The flip computation at parity.py:107 compares synthetic decisions on errored records against real model verdicts with no distinction, double-counting the same event under both criterion (b) and criterion (d)
An errored record with errored=True and valid=True produces a silent fabricated flip with no corroborating signal in existing metrics
Multiple arms with different numbers of genuine vs fabricated flips produce byte-identical gating-failure strings, making them indistinguishable to readers
The fix adds an errored guard reading a.errored or b.errored to decision_flips, counts excluded pairs into a new errored_pairs metric, and surfaces it in ParityReport.metrics and the gating string
Offline re-score of the recorded live run with the fix applied changes no metrics, confirming the fix does not affect the Bedrock verdict on clean data
